messages.text:
For both, the ECAL Si-W and LAr Layouts, make a single documentation PR that links and connects to the barrel / EC PRs and only summarizes the layout:
- overall envelope viewing and drawing (the layout drawing in rz)
- summary of the detector (including material, space and support budget)
- concise description of EC and barrel (with links to the PR)
- all in the description box of the PR (and separately as a 4 page pdf with identical content)

This is a central entry for the reviewers, not (yet) a TDR

I’ll create one documentation PR as the reviewer entry point for both layouts, linking the barrel and endcap PRs and summarizing their envelopes and material, space and support budgets. I’ll put the same content in the PR description and a four-page PDF, including both R–Z drawings.

I’m using the PDF skill and the repository’s coordination and evidence-review skills. I’ll have the documented layouts and budget claims checked while I prepare a common source for the PR description and PDF, so their content stays aligned.

All four ECAL component PRs are still open, so I’m basing this documentation PR on `main` and linking to their exact revisions. It can serve as the reviewer entry point independently of either implementation stack.

I’m also separating model mass from engineering estimates. The Si-W copper cooling plates and the LAr cryostat/support proxies contribute substantial material, so comparing the totals alone would be misleading.

The four-page overview is drafted, with matched PR text and PDF content. The R–Z drawings use the same axes for both layouts, and the budgets distinguish modeled material from reserved service space and engineering estimates. I’m checking the final claims against the linked component revisions before opening the documentation PR.

The final PDF has four pages, and the content check matches all text, tables, captions and links to the PR description. The summary highlights two review questions: the large Si-W copper cooling mass and the LAr service paths currently blocked by the rear support annulus. I’m completing the revision check and repository records now.

[PR #75](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/75) is open with the full overview in its description and the matching PDF. It links the Si-W barrel/endcap PRs #71/#70 and the LAr barrel/endcap PRs #73/#74. I’m finishing the final review and CI checks; the PR uses existing tools and adds no externals.

The comparison now shows the space impact clearly: the HCAL outline extends to a maximum corner radius of 3.833 m and a full length of 12.018 m for Si-W, versus 4.717 m and 15.712 m for LAr. The brief identifies these as envelope allocations; complete HCAL mass and support loads are still missing. The token-site preview has passed.

The final claim review found no material numerical or scope errors. It requested one small clarification: the Si-W endcap coverage figure comes from 360 azimuth rays and means active silicon in at least one layer. I’ve added that basis to both the PR text and PDF.

The document and review checks are complete. I caught a session-log format error during closeout: reviewer assessments were entered where the log expects command exit codes. I’m moving them to the narrative record and rerunning validation before finishing.

limitations: Only visible user/assistant text and exposed operation names/counts retained; reasoning, commands/results and arbitrary tool arguments excluded.
App response cap 4000 characters per item may truncate long visible messages; original curated journals and GitHub discussions retain their complementary evidence.
Conservative path, credential, email and URL redaction applied; no raw client rollout stored.
